title: VPC & On‑Prem Licensed Packaging: Credits, Support Bands, and SQ Response Matrix
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Design and validate a simple, sales-friendly licensed packaging model for VPC and on‑prem customers that balances predictable revenue (license fee), usage-linked capacity credits, and a clear support tier matrix tied to upgrade cadence. We also need a templated Security Questionnaire (SQ) response matrix aligned to each packaging offering so sales/legal can respond to enterprise RFPs quickly.

Background: customers deploying in VPC/on‑prem ask for (1) predictable license fees for baseline entitlement, (2) metered credits for burst/scale, (3) clear SLAs and an upgrade cadence that reduces churn risk, and (4) fast SQ turnaround. Current proposals in the wild are inconsistent and create negotiation overhead.

Key proposal elements (initial experiment):
- License fee: baseline node-equivalent license charged monthly or annually. Suggested anchoring: $15k/month per 8-GPU pool (list price placeholder). Offer a 10% discount for annual prepay.
- Capacity Credits: per-token or per-concurrency credits sold in packs (e.g., 250k token-equivalent pack / 1M token pack) that can be consumed by peak workloads. Unused credits expire on 12-month horizon.
- Support bands: Standard (business hours, 48h response), Priority (24/7 ticket triage, 4h P1 SLA), Enterprise (dedicated CSM, 1h P1 SLA, on-call escalation). Add an optional "Hotfix Support" add-on for guaranteed 24h patch turnaround.
- Upgrade cadence: three choices for customers to opt into: Fast (monthly security patches + quarterly minor updates), Balanced (monthly security patches + biannual minor updates), Conservative (security only patches + annual minor updates). Conservative customers pay a small premium to offset fragmentation risk.
- SQ Response Matrix: canonical answers for common self-serve questionnaire sections: infra isolation, encryption at rest/in transit, KMS/HSM integration, RBAC/audit logs, data residency, pen test cadence, SOC2/ISO artifacts. Map which artifacts are included at each support band and packaging tier.

Why an experiment? We need to A/B test whether (A) bundling capacity credits with license fee improves conversion and reduces renewal friction, and (B) offering explicit conservative upgrade cadence reduces support escalations but increases long-term maintenance cost.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Too many options -> sales paralysis. Keep options to 3 packaging tiers + 2 add-ons max.
- Conservative cadence increases surface area for forked security fixes; may require engineering gating and additional QE.
- Credit expiration and refund policy are negotiation points for large customers; legal needs guardrails.

Deliverables:
- Pricing matrix PDF for sales + 2 canned example proposals (SMB enterprise, regulated enterprise).
- SQ response spreadsheet (CSV + markdown) mapping question -> vetted answer -> artifact link.
- Pilot with 3 inbound customers (list of pilot customers to be attached in follow-ups).

Acceptance criteria and next steps are below.
acceptance_criteria: Sales collateral (pricing matrix + proposal templates) reviewed and approved by GTM and Legal
SQ response matrix complete for top 30 questionnaire items and approved by Security
Pilot contract signed with at least one customer on the new packaging within 6 weeks
Implementation runbook for conservative upgrade cadence created and engineering resource estimate validated
success_metrics: Time to close (RFP->contract) reduced by 30% for pilot customers
Number of SQ back-and-forth messages per deal reduced by 50% vs baseline
Renewal rate after 12 months for packaged customers >= 85%
Fewer than 2 ad-hoc engineering hotfix patches required per conservative-cadence customer per year during pilot
rollout_plan: Week 0-1: finalize pricing anchors and support language with Legal and Finance
Week 2: produce sales collateral and SQ canonical spreadsheet; hold Sales enablement workshop
Week 3-8: run 8-week pilot with 3 customers (varying regulated vs non-regulated), collect feedback
Week 9: review pilot, adjust packaging, and decide go/no-go for productization
